Analysis design fixed October 5, 2026 after reviewing earlier project results.
This is a specified follow-up, not a preregistration before research began.

POPULATION
Index events are the established pool/nonadjacent 24-month opportunities,
November 2023 through October 2025, excluding both author accounts.
The hash sample selects unordered numeric account pairs before outcomes or
future meetings are used. No realized-future-singleton restriction is used.
Histories include all sources in the five rated real-time speed categories.
They cannot establish whether participants knew one another off-platform,
in casual games, under other accounts, or in unrecorded contact.

TIME
utc_ms is the canonical recorded start; api_last_move_at_ms is lastMoveAt.
The latter is an anchor proxy, not a measured button-click timestamp.
A later encounter starts strictly after that anchor; the upper endpoint is
included. A window is eligible only if anchor + H days is strictly before
2025-11-01 00:00 UTC. Incomplete windows are not coded as no future encounter.
Later repayment opportunities must also have their own anchor within the
window. A one-hour-after-anchor encounter sensitivity is provided.
Prior counts use [start-H,start), with exact time ties excluded. A historical
first-pair minimum strictly before start marks repeat status. Ambiguous
first-meeting ties are reported and excluded from first/repeat regressions.
All projected focal games must match chronology game, pair, start and speed;
conflicts stop the run. Timestamps and account identifiers are not imputed.

REPAYMENT
For an original chooser A facing B, a return opportunity has B as chooser
and A as disconnected recipient. A later meeting alone is not repayment.
The preferred return universe is the all-source Stage07 panel, allowing
challenge and rematch opportunities. Active decisions only are observed;
waiting, casual play, chat and other favors are not measured.
The fallback universe is the main pool/nonadjacent panel and is labeled in
every repayment summary. It cannot bound omitted return opportunities.

The return benefit uses A's stored rating-state premium when A is the later
recipient, not B's cost of granting. Under the maintained fixed-state v2
formula this equals A's draw-minus-loss benefit. This is not a newly fitted
rating model and is not a statement that users perceive the exact quantity.
Summing this benefit over all observed reverse-role opportunities describes
the available rating repayment on the observed path if each were granted.
Missing values are counted; affected index rows are excluded only from
monetary summaries, remaining in event counts and rates. Sums are compared
with the initial cost among value-complete rows, separately for initial
grants, claims and the full index sample. Observed return counts may depend
on the initial action, and repeated index events can share later events.
This accounting is neither a causal upper bound nor a lifetime bound nor
an estimate of players' subjective expected returns.

PREDICTION
The label is any subsequent same-pair rated real-time game in 90 days.
Inputs available before the focal decision: both pregame ratings, rating
gap, prior-pair counts, earlier-meeting indicator, both participants' actual
30-day playing volume, fractions of that volume in the current UTC four-hour
slot, speed, time control, UTC slot, and prior-hour platform game volume in
the same speed. The latter is a density proxy, not an observed matching queue.
Current giving, board position, terminal clocks, and future outcomes are
not predictor features. Historical first meetings are measured in the
available archive and are not asserted to be first personal contact.

A ridge-regularized logistic model (penalty 1e-5 excluding intercept) is
trained on index games before May 2024 with labels mature before August 2024,
in pair folds 0/1. Features are standardized on training observations only.
The calibration set is August-October 2024, pair fold 2. Evaluation starts
November 2024, pair folds 3/4. All require complete 90-day coverage.
Pair folds use an independent salted stable hash; a pair never spans sets.
The low-risk cutoff is the twentieth percentile of calibration predictions.
It is fixed without inspecting grant outcomes or calibration outcome labels.
Calibration outcome labels are reported diagnostically; they are not used
to fit a calibration correction or select the cutoff. Thus some of those
diagnostic follow-up windows overlap evaluation dates without leaking their
labels into the fitted prediction or threshold.
Absolute prediction bands and observed evaluation meeting frequencies must
be examined before describing the lowest group as having negligible risk.
This predicts observed encounters under existing behavior, not encounters
under an intervention or subjective beliefs about being recognized.

REGRESSIONS
Linear probability models describe giving. Fixed effects: chooser, month,
speed, hour of week, and ply band. Controls: both ratings and rating deviations,
draw payoff, win premium, log remaining clocks and missing-clock indicators.
The first/repeat gradient model includes competitive, repeat, and their
interaction, on competitive or clearly-worse observations. The competitive
repeat-premium model adds evaluation-bin effects. Low-risk comparisons use
competitive versus clearly-worse positions in the held-out evaluation set,
and separately its first-recorded-meeting subset. These are associations.
The controls are not a claim of random pairing or exogenous meeting risk.
Nonfinite required numeric controls are counted and excluded per fit.

Chooser-clustered covariance uses the G/(G-1) group correction (labeled CR1),
without an additional absorbed-degree-of-freedom correction. It is reported
alongside a shared-account-or-date CR0
sensitivity: account-role aggregate meat minus unordered-pair meat, plus
date meat, minus account-date meat plus pair-date meat. Nonpositive or
non-PSD covariance is reported unsupported, not repaired. Prediction
uncertainty is not propagated; intervals condition on the trained rule.
Holm p-values cover three specified chooser-clustered tests: first-meeting
merit gradient, competitive repeat premium, and low-risk merit gradient.
Unavailable members remain in the family size. Other contrasts and
covariances are diagnostic; displayed 95% intervals are pointwise.

CLAIM LIMIT
Small re-encounter/repayment frequencies and persistence of granting at low
predicted risk can weaken particular strategic-return explanations. They
cannot eliminate recipient approval, spectators, chat, reputational beliefs,
off-platform benefits, or all external motives. No audience variable is
invented and missing audience information is never treated as zero.
